describes: rail-stroke.js buildStroke / laneProfile / laneAt / project / unproject / familyPartition / clipRangesToComplement
contract: One continuous polyline per part with the lane offset baked in through a triangular-kernel lane profile and its corners rounded; station anchors are the offset of their own vertex and are never trimmed. Pixel space in, pixel space out; the projection is pinned separately.

a corner split across near-coincident vertices is rounded as ONE corner to the minimum radius
the same split corner with no minimum radius: each vertex is rounded in isolation
a corner split coarser than the simplification tolerance is still rounded as ONE corner
the same coarse split corner with no minimum radius: each vertex is rounded in isolation
a station anchor inside a split corner is never swallowed by the run
a hairpin among near-coincident vertices is never rounded
joint before a reversal: the part that arrives, carrying the next part's lane and the joint's tangents
joint after a reversal: the part that leaves, carrying the previous part's lane and the same joint
followed joint: the part that arrives, its corridor follow reaching the shared vertex
followed joint: the part that leaves, its own corridor follow reaching the same vertex
followed joint: a stub shorter than the hold-back keeps its own survey entire
right angle on a station anchor: rounded through the anchor by an arc, the bead stays on the line
plateau shorter than the kernel is crossed, not held
hairpin reversal stays sharp; exact reversal uses the incoming normal
duplicate vertices collapse and anchors follow the survivor
two-point part: no interior, offset only
one-point part degenerates to a zero-length stroke
no rows, radius 0: the polyline passes through untouched
shallow bends under the fillet floor are left on their vertex
seam jog: a 30 m sideways step is tapered over 150 m either side
seam jog held back by a platform 60 m before it
a jog too small to be a seam (3 m) is left alone
a street S-bend of right angles is not a seam
offset fold: a two-pixel lane on a sub-pixel hairpin curve is unfolded
corridor follow: a weaving stroke is drawn from the canonical alignment, blended in and out
corridor follow against the digitised direction: canonical measures run backwards
two seam jogs 250 m apart: each gets its own taper and the windows meet without backing over each other
a platform at a corridor hand-over survives the substitution fold pass and its bead stays put
a single point still answers one anchor position per requested anchor
two lane rows starting at the same measure keep their input order
mitre limit: a 170° turn offsets by the clamped bisector
corridor follow onto a jogged canonical: the canonical's own seam jog is tapered before any follower draws from it
lane offset folds exactly at an anchor vertex: the bead is read from the surviving edge, not the discarded offset point
30 degree turn on a station anchor: rounded through the anchor by an arc, the bead stays on the line
a station anchor at a chain end is never filleted, whatever the radius asks for
a station anchor beside a very short edge still rounds through the anchor, the tangent capped by that edge
a 120 degree turn on a station anchor takes the reflex arc through the vertex
a 160 degree reversal at a station anchor is left unfilleted, whatever the radius asks for
a station anchor's tangent is clamped by the run-merged corner just before it, sharing a short edge

centripetal S curve

curved station by final measure
parallel lane on rounded centreline
